text: Q: Why does my code raise KeyError on dict access? A (accepted, 1.3k votes): the key is not present. Use d.get('k') which returns None instead of raising, or collections.defaultdict if you want a default factory. Wrapping in try/except KeyError also works when the miss is exceptional.

Q: pip says the package is installed but I still get ModuleNotFoundError. A (accepted, 2.1k votes): your 'pip' and 'python' point to different environments. Run 'python -m pip install NAME' and compare 'which python' with 'which pip'. Also check you did not shadow the package with a local file of the same name.

Q: RuntimeError: This event loop is already running (Jupyter). A (accepted, 800 votes): notebooks run their own loop; call 'import nest_asyncio; nest_asyncio.apply()' once, then await your coroutine. Do not call asyncio.run() inside the notebook.

Q: TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable. A (accepted, 950 votes): a function you call returns None, often a method that mutates in place like list.sort() or random.shuffle(). Capture the right value or fix the return.

Q: IndexError: list index out of range in a loop. A (accepted, 700 votes): you are indexing past the end; iterate with enumerate or guard with 'if i < len(xs)'. Off-by-one in range() is the usual cause.
Q: TabError: inconsistent use of tabs and spaces in indentation. A (accepted, 600 votes): set your editor to 'spaces' and run 'python -tt' to find the mix; reindent the block with 4 spaces.

Q: AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'group'. A (accepted, 1.1k votes): re.match / re.search return None when there is no match, so calling .group() on the result fails. Check 'if m:' before m.group().

Q: ImportError: cannot import name X from partially initialized module (most likely due to a circular import). A (accepted, 1.4k votes): two modules import each other. Move one import inside the function that needs it, or extract the shared piece into a third module.

Q: SyntaxError: 'await' outside function. A (accepted, 500 votes): await only works inside 'async def'. Put your awaits in an async function and run it with asyncio.run(main()), or use a notebook cell that supports top-level await.

Q: RuntimeWarning: coroutine was never awaited. A (accepted, 650 votes): you called an async function without awaiting it. Use 'await f()' inside async code, or 'asyncio.run(f())' at the top level; use asyncio.gather to run several.

Q: Removing items from a list while looping skips elements. A (accepted, 1.6k votes): mutating the list shifts the iterator. Loop over a copy 'for x in xs[:]', or better build a new list: xs = [x for x in xs if not drop(x)].

Q: ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: ''. A (accepted, 900 votes): int() got a non-integer string (empty, whitespace, or a decimal). Strip it, validate, or use int(float(s)) for decimals. Guard user input with try/except ValueError.

Q: TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'int' and 'str'. A (accepted, 1.2k votes): you mixed a number and a string. Use str(n) + s to build text, or int(s) + n to add. An f-string like f'{n}{s}' is usually cleanest.

Q: UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte. A (accepted, 3.2k votes): the file is not UTF-8. Open with the real encoding, e.g. open(path, encoding='latin-1') or 'cp1252'; if unsure, detect it (charset-normalizer) or pass errors='replace' to avoid the crash while noting you may lose characters.

Q: FileNotFoundError even though the file is right there. A (accepted, 1.0k votes): the path is relative to the working directory, not the script. Print os.getcwd(), use an absolute path or one built from __file__, and check Path(p).exists() first.

Q: My function's default list keeps its values between calls. A (accepted, 2.8k votes): default arguments are evaluated once at def time, so a default [] is shared across calls. Use acc=None and set acc=[] inside the function.

Q: KeyError: 'name' from str.format(). A (accepted, 400 votes): the template references {name} but you did not pass name=. Also escape literal braces as {{ and }}. Prefer f-strings when the values are local variables.

Q: RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration. A (accepted, 1.5k votes): you added or deleted keys while looping over the dict. Iterate over a snapshot: for k in list(d): or build a new dict; do not mutate d inside 'for k in d'.

Q: IndentationError: unexpected indent. A (accepted, 700 votes): a line is indented more than its block allows, often a stray space or a leftover indent after pasting. Align the line with its siblings; use a linter to catch it early.

Q: How do I actually isolate project dependencies so installs stop conflicting? A (accepted, 2.4k votes): use a virtual environment: 'python -m venv .venv' then activate it and install there. Never rely on global site-packages for a project; commit a requirements.txt so it is reproducible.
